reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every integer n >= 3, every real kappa >= 4, and every real ell >= 0, let G = O(n) be the full real orthogonal group and let mu be normalized Borel Haar probability on G. Write A(O) = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T). Define nu_+ = 2 mu restricted to {O in G : det O = 1} and nu_- = 2 mu restricted to {O in G : det O = -1}. For each O in G let gamma_O be the actual centered Gaussian law N(0,A(O)^{-1}) on Borel Euclidean R^n, and define the mixture measures P_+(B) = integral_G gamma_O(B) d nu_+(O) and P_-(B) = integral_G gamma_O(B) d nu_-(O) for every Borel set B. Put t_ell(x) = exp(-ell ||x||_2^2) and p_O(x) = sqrt(det A(O))/(2 pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A(O)x/2), with dx denoting Euclidean Lebesgue volume. Then
2 | integral_G det(O) [ integral_(R^n) t_ell(x) p_O(x) dx ] d mu(O) | <= sup_{B Borel subset R^n} |P_+(B)-P_-(B)|.
Here A(O) is positive definite, with every eigenvalue in [1,kappa]; nu_+, nu_-, gamma_O, and P_+, P_- are genuine probability measures, the family O -> gamma_O is measurable, and p_O is the actual volume density of gamma_O. These facts and the absolute integrability of both displayed integrals are consequences to be established internally, not extra hypotheses. The supremum is the real least upper bound of a nonempty bounded set of absolute event discrepancies. Its normalization is the event supremum, with no extra factor of two on the right. The case ell = 0 is included (the left side is then zero).
objects: G = O(n), normalized Haar probability mu on the whole group, the precision matrix A(O) = ((kappa+1)/2)I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), determinant-sign restrictions nu_+ and nu_-, canonical centered Gaussian laws gamma_O = N(0,A(O)^(-1)), their actual measure-bind mixtures P_+ and P_-, the radial tilt t_ell(x) = exp(-ell ||x||_2^2), and the actual Gaussian density p_O(x) = sqrt(det A(O))/(2 pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A(O)x/2).
domains: n is natural with n >= 3; kappa and ell are real. O ranges over all real n by n orthogonal matrices, including both determinant components. x ranges over EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), identified with R^n with its standard Euclidean norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Inner integration uses Euclidean volume; outer integration uses normalized Borel Haar measure mu. B ranges over every measurable (Borel) subset of this Euclidean space. The supremum is in R.
quantifiers: For every n in N with 3 <= n, for every kappa in R with 4 <= kappa, and for every ell in R with 0 <= ell, define mu, nu_+, nu_-, gamma, P_+, P_-, t and p as displayed and assert the inequality. The outer integral binds O; each inner integral binds x at the fixed O. The right-hand supremum ranges over all z in R for which there exists a measurable B subset R^n with z = |P_+(B)-P_-(B)|; equivalently it ranges over all measurable events B.
assumptions: The only parameter hypotheses are n >= 3, kappa >= 4 and ell >= 0. The orthogonality of O is its domain condition. Normalized Haar measure and the canonical multivariate Gaussian construction have the meanings fixed by the supplied definition context. Measurability of the Gaussian family, probability of its laws and mixtures, positive definiteness of A(O), density-to-law correspondence, absolute integrability, and nonemptiness/boundedness of the supremum set must be established internally; they are not assumed as additional hypotheses.
conclusion: 2 times the absolute value of integral over G of det(O) times [integral over R^n of exp(-ell ||x||_2^2) sqrt(det A(O))/(2 pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A(O)x/2) dx], against mu, is at most sup over Borel B subset R^n of |P_+(B)-P_-(B)|. P_+ and P_- are the Gaussian mixtures for nu_+ = 2 mu|_{det=1} and nu_- = 2 mu|_{det=-1}, respectively. This also equals |integral t_ell dP_+ - integral t_ell dP_-| <= the event supremum, since the signed mixture difference has the displayed factor 2.
scopes: All let-defined objects are local to the universally quantified parameters; mu and nu_+/nu_- depend on n, gamma and P_+/P_- additionally depend on kappa, and t depends on ell. A(O)^(-1) is the matrix inverse and is the covariance of gamma_O; A(O) is its precision. sqrt applies to the scalar determinant of A(O). All real integrals are actual absolutely integrable Bochner integrals. P_+(B), P_-(B) denote real-valued masses of the actual bind measures. The supremum is total variation distance in the event-supremum convention, not the total mass of signed variation. ell = 0 remains in scope, giving t identically 1 and a zero left side. No assertion is made outside n >= 3, kappa >= 4, ell >= 0.
scopes_senses: Full-group Haar probability retains both determinant signs. Restriction and multiplication by 2 give normalized sign-component probabilities, rather than a single-component Haar measure substituted for mu. Bind is the actual join of the pushed-forward Gaussian family. The inner unannotated integral is against Euclidean volume. Absolute value applies after the whole outer integral; the factor 2 lies outside it. The right supremum includes all measurable events, including the empty set, and is bounded by 1.
constant_dependencies: There are no unspecified constants and no existential constants. The factors 2, 1/2, 1/4, pi, and exponent n/2 are fixed exactly as displayed. The factor 2 in nu_+ and nu_- is the component normalization and the factor 2 before the absolute outer integral is exact. n, kappa and ell vary independently subject only to their stated bounds; no hidden dependence, asymptotic range, small-ell condition, or parameter-dependent multiplicative constant is present.
